subject: general
question: By which of the following Acts did the rule of the East India Company end in India, and the rule of the crown begin?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Government of India Act of 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Government of India Act of 1858 was enacted by the British Parliament in the wake of the Indian Rebellion of 1857.
 
• This Act marked the end of the East India Company's rule in India and the beginning of direct rule by the British Crown.
 
• The Act provided for the liquidation of the East India Company and the transfer of its functions to the British Crown.
 
• It established the office of the Secretary of State for India and the Council of India to assist the Secretary of State.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regulating Act of 1773:**

 
 
• This was the first attempt to regulate the affairs of the East India Company in India and establish a system of control over its administration.
 
• It provided for the appointment of a Governor-General of Bengal and four councillors to assist him.
 
 
 
• **Pitt's India Act of 1784:**
 
 
• Also known as the East India Company Act, this Act was introduced by the British Prime Minister William Pitt the Younger.
 
• It provided for the establishment of a Board of Control to oversee the civil, military, and revenue affairs of the Company in India.
 
 
 
• **Charter Act of 1813:**
 
 
• This Act ended the trade monopoly of the East India Company in India, except for trade in tea and trade with China.
 
• It allowed missionaries to come to India to spread Christianity and permitted local subjects to receive education.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act of 1853:**
 
 
• This Act was the last of the series of Charter Acts passed by the British Parliament.
 
• It introduced an open competition system for the selection of civil servants and separated the legislative and executive functions of the Governor-General's Council.
